newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SASOL RISES IN HEAVY VOLUMES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SASOL RISES IN HEAVY VOLUMES.

text.p: South African fuel-from-coal producer Sasol Ltd saw exceptionally heavy trade in several foreign deals on Thursday, propelling the day's stock market turnover to above average daily takings by noon.
By 1055 GMT nearly five million Sasol shares worth over 289 million rand had changed hands, taking the price up 100 cents to 59.25 rand.
Dealers said that the bulk of the shares appeared to be moving offshore although good two-way trade and one large asset swap had also taken place.
"Our analyst has said Sasol looks cheap at these levels," said a trader at one of the broking houses involved in several of the deals.
"It is also a good rand-hedge," the dealer added.
A rising dollar on international markets has pushed the rand to its weakest level in seven months.
Market rumours that Thursday's volume was due to South Africa's Industrial Development Corp (IDC) selling down its stake in Sasol also surfaced.
But, while the IDC said some of the trade could be down to them, it would not account for the heavy volumes.
"We have started to disinvest, but if any of those shares (traded on Thursday) are ours it would be less than 500,000," said Gert Gouws, IDC's finance general manager.
Gouws said the firm had started a gradual sell-down in Sasol about a year ago and regularly sold shares to finance its operations and if the market price was right.
Overall market turnover had soared to over 800 million rand by noon. On an average day around 750 million rand's worth of shares trade.
